name: Martin Sokk

education.school: Estonian Information Technology College (IT Kolledž), Tallinn
education.notes: Confirmed across multiple sources (LinkedIn-derived summaries, Crunchbase). Vocational/applied tech degree rather than a research university — typical Estonian product-engineer path.

keyDecisions: Took a first job inside Estonia's flagship energy utility post-degree rather than chasing a startup role — built product/process discipline inside a slow-moving incumbent.
lessons: Estonia's small market lets an ambitious operator rotate through the country's flagship incumbents in their early 20s and still be at a fintech rocket-ship by 27.
Time inside a non-tech incumbent forces you to learn the unsexy mechanics of regulated industries — useful preparation for later building regulated fintech.
careerSteps.notes: Per sTARTUp Day interview and search-derived summaries: Sokk worked at Eesti Energia (state energy utility) before Swedbank. Exact dates not publicly disclosed.

keyDecisions: Moved from an energy incumbent to a banking incumbent — got close to consumer financial products from inside the system he'd eventually build alternatives to.
lessons: Time inside an incumbent in your eventual disruption target is a cheap MBA in what's actually broken.
Banking-incumbent product reps are surprisingly portable into fintech — the regulated-product vocabulary is the same.
careerSteps.notes: Swedbank is one of the largest banks in the Baltic region. Exact dates not publicly disclosed; sequence is pre-Wise per the founder's own framing.

careerSteps.role: First Product Hire / Head of Product
keyDecisions: Joined TransferWise as the first product person — bet on the Estonia-to-global fintech playbook before it was obvious.
Built and ran Wise's product organisation through hypergrowth — direct apprenticeship under a generational founding team.
Left Wise in 2020 (before the July 2021 direct listing) to start a consumer-facing fintech rather than waiting for IPO liquidity.
lessons: Being the first product hire at a generational company is the closest thing to a founder apprenticeship — you absorb the operating system without bearing the founding risk.
Liquidity from IPO is not always worth the opportunity cost of two more years inside someone else's company.
The Wise alumni network is now a structural advantage for Estonian fintech founders — the 'Wise-mafia' is real.
careerSteps.notes: Sokk describes himself in Lightyear's own blog as 'a lifelong product builder in the finance world having joined Wise as the first product person.' Specific dates not publicly disclosed; he reconnected with co-founder Mihkel Aamer (also Wise alumnus) in summer 2020.

keyDecisions: Co-founded Lightyear in October 2020 with Mihkel Aamer (CTO) — applied the Wise customer-centric / transparent-pricing playbook to retail investing.
Headquartered in London for FCA / regulatory access while keeping core team Estonian — classic Wise-style dual geography.
Took a patient regulatory path — operated for years before securing UK FCA licence in 2024.
At the FCA-licence milestone in 2024, brought in Wander Rutgers as UK CEO and stepped back into a group-CEO role.
lessons: Applying a proven fintech playbook (Wise's transparent-pricing customer-centricity) to an adjacent regulated vertical is a tractable second-act for Wise alumni.
Regulated fintech rewards patience — FCA licensing in 2024 came four years after founding.
Hire your replacement at the regulatory-milestone moment; group CEO + local CEO is a sustainable structure for pan-European fintech.
careerSteps.notes: Raised ~$25M Series A led by Lightspeed in 2022 with Richard Branson as angel; reportedly raised a further ~$23M in 2025. Now operates across ~25 European countries.

outcomes.currentStatus: Group CEO and co-founder of Lightyear, a pan-European neobroker operating in ~25 countries. Based in London with core team in Tallinn.

lessons.lesson: Customer-centric product thinking + technology-driven cost reduction (Wise playbook) can be applied to underserved adjacent verticals like retail investing.
IT Kolledž → incumbents (Eesti Energia, Swedbank) → first product hire at Wise → own fintech is a repeatable Estonian fintech ladder.
Estonia → London is a repeatable European fintech path: small-country product discipline + UK regulatory access.
Hire your replacement at the regulatory-milestone moment; group CEO + local CEO is a sustainable structure for pan-European fintech.
